stories.headline: Prosperity recovered faster than wellbeing
stories.insight: 4 of 143 countries with complete data grew real GDP per person while reported life satisfaction fell below its 2019 level. Tajikistan grew +38.7% in real GDP per person while life satisfaction moved -0.06 points.

stories.headline: Digital access expanded while life satisfaction weakened
stories.insight: 4 countries gained more than 10 percentage points of internet participation since 2019 while life satisfaction still sits below its pre-pandemic level. Ghana added +50.1 points of internet participation, the widest gap between digital growth and wellbeing decline in the sample.

stories.headline: Health outcomes held steady despite economic pressure
stories.insight: 4 countries recorded real GDP per person below its 2019 level while life expectancy still rose or held flat. Afghanistan's real GDP per person is -32.9% against 2019, yet life expectancy moved +3.3 years.

stories.headline: A small group of countries recovered on all four signals
stories.insight: Only 6 of 143 countries with any data show non-negative movement in LIVE, THRIVE, CONNECT and FEEL simultaneously — broad recovery was the exception, not the rule. India leads the group.

stories.headline: Middle East & North Africa shows the widest recovery spread of any region
stories.insight: Within Middle East & North Africa, real GDP per person ranges from -33.1% at Lebanon to +19.2% at Malta against the same 2019 baseline — one region, very different recoveries.
stories.region: Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan & Pakistan
